name: xTool S1 20W
tagline: Enclosed 20W diode: safer home engraving with moderate cutting
tldr: The 20W S1 is the value pick in xTool's enclosed diode line: same cabinet and filters as the 40W, but less cut depth on thick wood. Buy this if safety matters and you mostly engrave.

priceRange.note: Official xTool store, Oct 2026: $1,299 to $2,599 depending on bundle

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Balanced head: 10 mm basswood plywood and 8 mm black acrylic in one pass (xTool rating)
Spot of 0.08 × 0.06 mm per xTool keeps photo and text detail sharp
Cheapest S1 bundle on xTool's US store in October 2026 ($1,299 Basic)

editorialDepth.advantages: The 20W S1 is the sweet spot for apartment makers who want enclosure safety without paying for 40W cut headroom. You keep xTool's guided software, optional filter packs, and the same upgrade path as heavier SKUs. For coasters, leather, slate, and filled photos, the job quality matches the 40W module when you run sensible speeds.
editorialDepth.limitations: Thick hardwood, fast sign cutting, and clear acrylic production still push you toward the 40W head or a CO₂ machine. Photo work at gallery-grade density can take longer than on a dedicated low-watt engraving module. Budget for filter replacements or window ducting if you cut daily.

cons: Dense hardwoods such as beech, oak and bamboo need several passes
About 9 mm/s on 3 mm basswood: batch cutting takes noticeably longer than on the top head
Clear acrylic is out of reach, as with every diode
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W SKU on xTool S1. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other modules via the chips before buying.
proTips: Use air assist for cuts, lower scan speed for photo engraving. Multiple passes at moderate speed beat one aggressive pass. Check the flagship tier’s cut benchmark if you quote production times to customers.

faq.question: What can the xTool S1 20W cut in one pass?
faq.answer: xTool rates the 20W head for 10 mm basswood plywood, 10 mm cherry or walnut and 8 mm black acrylic in one pass, and 9 mm/s on 3 mm basswood. Expect those figures with air assist and a clean, flat sheet. In our benchmark a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood took about 5–8 min.

faq.question: S1 20W or 40W: which one should I buy?
faq.answer: Take the 20W if most jobs are engraving (coasters, leather, slate, photos) with occasional cuts up to about 6 mm. Take the 40W if you cut signs, boxes or 10 mm stock every week: xTool rates it 15 mm basswood plywood in one pass and 15 mm/s on 3 mm. On xTool's US store the Basic bundles were $1,299 and $1,699 in October 2026, a $400 gap.

faq.question: Can I add the 40W head to a 20W S1 later?
faq.answer: Yes. The heads swap on the same cabinet, and xTool sold the 40W module alone for $1,099 in October 2026. That is about $700 more than the bundle gap, so if you already expect to cut thick wood, buying the 40W upfront is cheaper.

mainObjective: Everyday engraving plus reliable light cutting on wood, leather, and dark acrylic

moduleSystem.headline: Interchangeable laser heads on the same S1 cabinet
moduleSystem.description: The xTool S1 is sold with different diode modules (10W, 20W, or 40W) or as a bare cabinet: heads swap with two screws and a plug. An optional 2W 1064 nm infrared module adds metal marking without a full fiber galvo. This is not a “hybrid” machine: you replace one head at a time.

standoutFeatures.title: 10 mm basswood in one pass
standoutFeatures.body: xTool rates the 20W head for 10 mm basswood plywood and 8 mm black acrylic in a single pass, enough for boxes, ornaments and dark acrylic lettering.

standoutFeatures.title: Lowest-priced S1 bundle
standoutFeatures.body: The 20W Basic bundle was $1,299 on xTool's US store in October 2026 and keeps the full S1 cabinet, safety features and LightBurn support.
